In [[mathematical analysis]], '''Strichartz estimates''' are a family of inequalities for linear [[dispersive partial differential equation]]s.  These inequalities establish size and decay of solutions in [[mixed norm]] [[Lp space|Lebesgue spaces]].  They were first noted by [[Robert Strichartz]] and arose out of connections to the Fourier restriction problem.<ref>{{citation|author=R.S. Strichartz|title=Restriction of Fourier Transform to Quadratic Surfaces and Decay of Solutions of Wave Equations|journal=Duke Math. J.|volume=44|year=1977|issue=3 |pages=705–713|doi=10.1215/s0012-7094-77-04430-1}}</ref>

== Examples ==
Consider the linear [[Schrödinger equation]] in <math>\mathbb{R}^d</math> with ''h''&nbsp;=&nbsp;''m''&nbsp;=&nbsp;1.  Then the solution for initial data <math>u_0</math> is given by <math>e^{it\Delta/2}u_0</math>.  Let ''q'' and ''r'' be real numbers satisfying <math>2\leq q, r \leq \infty</math>; <math>\frac{2}{q}+\frac{d}{r}=\frac{d}{2}</math>; and <math>(q,r,d)\neq(2,\infty,2)</math>.  

In this case the homogeneous Strichartz estimates take the form:<ref name=tao2006>{{citation|author=Tao, Terence|author-link=Terence Tao|title=Nonlinear dispersive equations: Local and global analysis|series=CBMS Regional Conference Series in Mathematics|volume=106|year=2006|isbn=978-0-8218-4143-3}}</ref>
:<math>\|e^{it\Delta/2} u_0\|_{L^q_tL^r_x}\leq C_{d,q,r} \|u_0\|_{L^2_x}.</math> 
Further suppose that <math>\tilde q, \tilde r</math> satisfy the same restrictions as <math>q, r</math> and <math>\tilde q', \tilde r'</math> are their dual exponents, then the dual homogeneous Strichartz estimates take the form:<ref name=tao2006 />
:<math>\left\| \int_\mathbb{R} e^{-is\Delta/2}F(s)\,ds\right\|_{L^2_x}\leq C_{d,\tilde q, \tilde r}\|F\|_{L^{\tilde q'}_tL^{\tilde r'}_x}.</math>

The inhomogeneous Strichartz estimates are:<ref name=tao2006 />
:<math>\left\| \int_{s<t} e^{i(t-s)\Delta/2}F(s)\,ds\right\|_{L^q_tL^r_x}\leq C_{d, q,  r, \tilde q, \tilde r}\|F\|_{L^{\tilde q'}_tL^{\tilde r'}_x}.</math>
